title: Logical BRAINK computer identity survives physical host migration
classification: logical computer identity / migration / semantic virtualization
statement: A logical BRAINK computer identity and its required persistent state can be reconstructed on a different physical host without redefining that logical identity.
invariants: logical computer identifier is independent of hostname, machine-id, IP address and transport endpoint
required persistent state is preserved across host replacement
carrier-specific identifiers remain projections rather than logical identity

falsification.experiment: Instantiate a logical computer on host A, persist its governed state, reconstruct it on independent host B, and verify the same logical identifier, state digest, lineage and authority while machine/transport identifiers differ.
falsification.pass_condition: Host A and host B present the same logical computer identity and required state/authority invariants while exposing different machine/carrier identities.
falsification.fail_condition: Logical identity changes with hostname/machine-id/IP, required state cannot be reconstructed, or authority/lineage diverges.

proof_requirements.description: Capture logical identity, state, lineage and authority on host A.
Reconstruct the same logical computer on independent host B.
External consumer resolves and interacts with the logical identity after migration.
Repeat migration/rehydration without logical identity drift.

invalid_overclaims: Current remote_fabric_node node_id is not proof of this claim because it includes machine_material().
A same-host process restart is not cross-host migration.
A carrier endpoint change is not physical-host replacement.
Queued independent-host CI is not cross-machine evidence.
next_experiments: Bind R31 persisted state/lineage to LogicalComputerIdentity.
Execute controlled A-to-B host migration with signed receipts.
